rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This continues the pattern of Noah’s people failing to believe and fear God; the conjunction makes this account a stronger consolation for the Prophet.
rows.anchor: فلم يؤمنوا ولم يتقوا داب قوم نوح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-malaʾ are the eminent chiefs whose appearance fills the onlookers’ chests.
rows.anchor: أي الإشراف الذين تملأ رؤيتهم الصدور

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting “from his people” first emphasizes and specifies the consolation; it also avoids placing it after the long relative clause.
rows.anchor: اهتماما وتخصيصا للإبلاغ في التسلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their disbelief means they covered up what they knew from the proofs of divine oneness and the punishment of idolaters.
rows.anchor: غطوا ما يعرفون من أدلة التوحيد والانتقام من المشركين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial of meeting the Hereafter is denial of resurrection.
rows.anchor: لتكذيبهم بالبعث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Worldly luxury, often mistaken for happiness, usually blocks afterlife felicity by fostering insolence, ingratitude, and arrogance even toward the Benefactor.
rows.anchor: قاطع في الغالب عن سعادة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They point to the Messenger with “this” to belittle him before their audience.
rows.anchor: أشاروا إليه تحقيرا له عند المخاطبين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They allege that he resembles them in creation and condition, implying no distinction that could make him a messenger.
rows.anchor: أي في الخلق والحال

words: يَأْكُلُ مِمَّا تَأْكُلُونَ مِنْهُ وَيَشْرَبُ مِمَّا تَشْرَبُونَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They cite his eating ordinary food and drinking ordinary drink to argue that he cannot be a messenger above them.
rows.anchor: من شرابها فكيف يكون رسولا دونكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say obeying a human they regard as their equal would make the followers dupes for preferring him over themselves despite rejecting his claim.
rows.anchor: أي مغبونون لكونكم فضلتم مثلكم عليكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They describe death as souls separating from bodies, with dust covering the flesh beneath the bones until only bare bones remain.
rows.anchor: ففارقت أرواحكم أجسادكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second “that you will be brought out” replaces the first “that you” to clarify what is promised after their souls have been stirred by the preceding description.
rows.anchor: مبدلا من { أنكم } الأولى إيضاحا للمعنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being brought out means leaving that state and returning to life in the bodies they had before.
rows.anchor: أي من تلك الحالة التي صرتم إليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repeating “far, far” marks the promised resurrection as extremely remote, to the point they deem it impossible.
rows.anchor: أي بعد بعد جدا بحيث صار ممتنعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase “for what you are promised” is cut off from the preceding construction to magnify their emphatic rejection; an implied question asks what prompted it.
rows.anchor: بل قطع عنه تفخيما له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their emphatic denial that resurrection is possible leads directly to the claim that worldly life is the only life they can have.
rows.anchor: في التبعيد كأنهم قالوا : إنا لا نبعث أصلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They explain worldly life as some people dying while new people are born after them.
rows.anchor: أي يموت منا من هو موجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They deny being raised after death.
rows.anchor: بعد الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They reduce Noah’s message to a lie and call him a man who deliberately fabricated falsehood against God; the author also allows that they mean he is one man and unworthy of notice.
rows.anchor: الرجل لا ينبغي مثل ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say they do not believe him concerning resurrection or his being a messenger.
rows.anchor: أي بمصدقين فيما يخبرنا به من البعث والرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Noah calls on the Lord who favored him by sending and nurturing him, asking for victory over those who rejected him.
rows.anchor: بإرسالي إليهم وغيره من أنواع التربية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God promises that they will soon regret failing to follow Noah; the added particle ما intensifies the shortness of the time.
rows.anchor: وأكد قلته بزيادة ( ما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their destruction follows Noah’s prayer, fulfilling God’s promise to him.
rows.anchor: أن تعقب هلاكهم , وعد الله له بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cry may be so powerful that it is the only cry of its kind, specifically Gabriel’s cry against Thamud, or it may figuratively mean terrible punishment.
rows.anchor: ويمكن أن تكون على بابها فتكون صيحة جبرئيل عليه الصلاة والسلام ويكون القوم ثمود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment was an established, deserved judgment that no one but God could repel, and it was just.
rows.anchor: بالأمر الثابت من العذاب الذي أوجب لهم الذي لا تمكن مدافعته لهم ولا لأحد غير الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They lay dead like hollow palm trunks and were cast aside like flood debris: vegetation carried by a torrent that blackens, decays, and becomes useless.
rows.anchor: يطرحون كما يطرح الغثاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God saved their messenger and the believers; the unbelievers perished, while believers prospered and inherited the land.
rows.anchor: ونجينا رسولهم ومن معه من المؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invocation of distance means destruction and expulsion.
rows.anchor: أي هلاكا وطردا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text states the blameworthy quality instead of a pronoun, making the warning general; these powerful people had no excuse and misused their strength by failing to support the messengers.
rows.anchor: أظهر الضمير تعميما وتعليقا للحكم بالوصف تحذيرا لكل من تلبس به

words: ثُمَّ أَنشَأْنَا مِن بَعْدِهِمْ قُرُونًا ءَاخَرِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In answer to their taunt that destruction would come too late, and to the Arabs’ claim that generational death and renewal never cease, God created further generations after Noah and the generation following him.
rows.anchor: من بعد من قدمنا ذكره من نوح والقرن الذي بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: No nation can precede or outlast its appointed term; the present tense signals this never happened and never will, and من makes the statement universal.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى أنه ما كان شيء من ذلك ولا يكون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Elsewhere the order is reversed and delay comes first, because those passages assume the term has arrived and focus on whether it can be delayed.
rows.anchor: وعكس هذا الترتيب في غيرها من الآيات فقدم الاستئخار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After creating each generation and allowing it a long reprieve, God sent messengers in succession; this implies an interval between every two messengers, and “our” adds majesty and consolation.
rows.anchor: أن بين كل رسولين فترة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi derives tatra from the bowstring, evoking successive items joined together.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : من وتر القوس لاتصاله

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi explains the related expression as following one another with a short interval between reports.
rows.anchor: واترت الخبر : اتبعت بعضه بعضا

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani says the original form was watrā, with wāw changed to tā as in taqwā.
rows.anchor: فقلبت الواو تاء كما قلبوها في التقوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Each messenger came calling his people to worship God alone, with no other deity.
rows.anchor: فجاء كل رسول إلى أمته قائلا : اعبدوا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger is attributed to his own nation to rebuke them for refusing the honor and to console the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ذما لهم لأن يخصوا بالكرامة فيأبوها ولقصد التسلية أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb is assigned to the whole nation because most people in each nation denied its messenger.
rows.anchor: الأكثر من كل أمة مكذبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed successive peoples all at once by varied punishments, such as a cry, earthquake, or swallowing; the differing fates and believers’ rescue show deliberate divine action, not time, in response to denial.
rows.anchor: بعضهم بالصيحة , وبعضهم بالرجفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They became stories people recount and marvel at, warning the perceptive that unbelievers fail and believers do not lose.
rows.anchor: أي أخبارا يسمر بها ويتعجب منها ليكونوا عظة للمستبصرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their destruction is invoked because their nature is so unbalanced that they never come to faith, even as the seasons pass.
rows.anchor: وإن جرت عليهم الفصول الأربعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the miraculous eloquence and wisdom of the signs should invite acceptance after reflection, their turning away and calling them magic, poetry, or soothsaying prompts this rebuke.
rows.anchor: تارة بالسحر وأخرى بالشعر , وكره بالكهانة ومرة بغيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: To reflect on the speech is to inspect its aftermath and consequences; it warrants acceptance, attachment, and the finest praise.
rows.anchor: أي المتلو عليهم بأن ينظروا في أدباره وعواقبه ولو لم يبلغوا في نظرهم الغاية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling the revelation “speech” suggests that someone who will not accept it is unfit to understand speech at all, like a beast.
rows.anchor: لعله عبر بالقول إشارة إلى أن من لم يتقبله ليس بأهل لفهم شيء من القول بل هو في عداد البهائم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The new message brings monotheism and commands whose benefits are obvious to the rational, along with prohibitions whose ugliness even the ignorant can recognize; its bearer descends from Ishmael and Abraham.
rows.anchor: من الأوامر بالتوحيد الآتي بها الرسول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s audience cannot reject the message simply as something wholly alien to the generations before them.
rows.anchor: ما لم يأت آباءهم الأولين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They know the Messenger’s lineage, truthfulness, trustworthiness, and outstanding character, with no fault to name even after scrutiny; Abu Sufyan’s account to Heraclius in Bukhari supports this.
rows.anchor: كما دلت عليه الأحاديث الصحاح منها حديث أبي سفيان بن حرب رضي الله عنه الذي في أول البخاري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they deny him or his message from ignorance of his state, they attain neither the rank of discerning critics nor of followers; they know he is exceptionally truthful yet deny him.
rows.anchor: فلم يحرز شيئا من رتبتي الناس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They suggest their Messenger is insane and therefore untrustworthy, since he might speak confusedly in a way whose flaw is hidden at first.
rows.anchor: فلا يوثق به لأنه قد يخلط فيأتي بما فيه مطعن وإن خفي وجه الكعن فيه الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The insanity charge is untenable: they know him as perfect in character and morals, pure in disposition, resolute, sound in judgment, truthful in speech, and correct in action.
rows.anchor: الرسول الكريم وأنه أكملهم خلقا , واشرفهم خلقا , وأطهرهم شيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After dismissing attacks on the message and its bearer, the author says their rejection comes from stubbornness, not the supposed defects.
rows.anchor: اضرب عنها وقال : { بل } أي لم ينكصوا عند سماع الآيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger brought unimpeachable truth, with the clearest monotheism and rulings; the Qur’an’s challenge, which they could not meet, makes this plain to a fair person.
rows.anchor: أبين مما فيه من التوحيد والأحكام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most hate the truth out of stubbornness and attachment to base desires; some reject it through ignorance, imitation, or fear of being called a convert, while others follow by God’s guidance and support.
rows.anchor: متابعة للأهواء الرديئة والشهوات البهيمية عنادا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If they stopped hating the truth, they would love and follow it, becoming upright and reforming themselves; the hypothetical explains the consequence of their aversion.
rows.anchor: فلو تركوا الكره لأحبوه ولو أحبوه لأتبعوه ولو اتبعوه لانصلحوا وأصلحوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author allows the conditional clause to function as a circumstantial clause after “hating,” as Shaykh Saʿd al-Din discusses, or as a conjunction with an implied preceding condition and result.
rows.anchor: ولعله حال من فاعل كاره , فإن جزاءه خبري مسوغ لكونه حالا كما ذكره الشيخ سعد الدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following their whims would ruin creation: multiple gods entail mutual obstruction, and conflicting desires cause disputes and harm until truth restores order by wisdom and subdues them.
rows.anchor: لأدى ببرهان التمانع إلى الفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their reminder is the wise Book, which repairs knowledge and order: reflection frees the ignorant from ignorance and guides their conduct, while leading the learned toward perfection and honor.
rows.anchor: وهو الكتاب الذي في غاية الحكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Book would bring them honor and renown, so their turning away from it only harms them; their rejection brings no loss to God.
rows.anchor: إنما ضرره عائد إليهم , وراجع في كل حال عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After refuting their objections about the message and Messenger, the author points out that they know he asks no payment, removing another possible suspicion.
rows.anchor: إذا انتفت وجوه المطاعن

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi glosses kharj as payment or a reward.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : أجرا وجعلا

rows.speaker: ابن مكتوم
rows.claim: Ibn Maktum says kharj and kharaj can be an annual, measured levy from communal wealth; kharaj can also mean a slave’s or bondwoman’s earnings.
rows.anchor: الخرج والخراج شيء يخرجه القوم في السنة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj distinguishes kharaj as fayʾ from kharj as a tax or jizya.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج : الخراج : الفيء

rows.speaker: الأصبهاني
rows.claim: Al-Asbahani transmits Abu Amr ibn al-Ala’s distinction: kharaj is an obligatory payment, whereas kharj is a voluntary gift.
rows.anchor: شئل أبو عمرو بن العلاء فقال : الخراج ما لزمك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s reward is better than payment from them because it is never cut off or withheld, even from sinners; calling it a due payment hints that God has pledged every servant’s provision without fail.
rows.anchor: لأن خراجه غير مقطوع ولا ممنوع عن أحد من عباده المسيئين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows what benefits or harms each recipient and provides accordingly, without making anyone ask.
rows.anchor: ما يصلح كل مرزوق وما يفسده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The arguments have removed all objections; the Prophet’s call is true and ennobling, especially because it comes from the King of kings through the most devoted and noble of creation.
rows.anchor: خالصة العباد وأشرف الخلق , كما قام عليه الدليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet’s reminder calls them, despite every refuted objection, to a straight path with no crookedness or valid flaw; sound minds attest to it, and following it reaches the goal and every honor.
rows.anchor: فقال عاطفا على { آتيناهم } : { وإنك } أي مع انتفاء هذه المطاعن كلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they do not fear reckoning in the Hereafter, they stray from the only path that reaches the destination; the wording may also mean a path described as straight.
rows.anchor: أي الذي لا صراط غيره لأنه لا موصل إلى القصد غيره

words: وَلَوْ رَحِمْنَٰهُمْ وَكَشَفْنَا مَا بِهِم مِّن ضُرٍّۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their cry for relief is temporary and not genuine guidance: even if God removed their distress, they would persist blindly in the transgression they had before it.
rows.anchor: أنه لا اعتداد به لعروضه

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir treats this as God’s knowledge of what would happen if an unrealized condition were to occur.
rows.anchor: قال ابن كثير : فهذا من باب علمه بما لا يكون

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reports Ibn Abbas’s view that every Qur’anic statement using law describes something that never happens.
rows.anchor: قال الضحاك عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما : كل ما فيه ( لو )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question is a rebuke spoken to the punished: God’s signs had been recited to them in worldly life, but they persisted in denying them.
rows.anchor: أي يقال لهم في تأنيبهم وتوبيخهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The signs are described as reaching the highest rank because they are attributed to God.
rows.anchor: التي انتهى عظمها إلى أعلى المراتب بإضافتها إلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive construction highlights that the signs’ mere recitation should have sufficed for belief.
rows.anchor: نبه على ذلك بالبناء للمفعول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Putting “in them” before “you denied” emphasizes how persistently they rejected the signs that should have led them to faith.
rows.anchor: قدم الظرف للإعلام بمبالغتهم في التكذيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They say their wretchedness overcame them, meaning their desires led them into evil deeds that became the apparent cause of misery.
rows.anchor: أهواؤنا التي قادتنا إلى سوء الأعمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were a people astray from guidance and steeped in causes of misery, as if captive to them and driven by devils.
rows.anchor: المأسورين , تؤزنا إليها الشياطين أزا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Having admitted fault in a way that might invite mercy, they ask God to release them from Hell and return them to worldly life so they can act as He desires.
rows.anchor: هذا الإقرار الاعتذار , وكان ذلك ربما شوغ الخلاص

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They promise that if they return to the same deviations, they will indeed be wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: فإنا ظالمون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: “Be gone” is a rebuke like driving away a dog; they are to remain silent in Hell in humiliation, unworthy of God’s address.
rows.anchor: انطردوا عن مخاطبيت ساكتين سكوت هوان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God refuses their request because they remained characterized by injustice, including this request, which implies they would return to wrongdoing if released.
rows.anchor: لأنكم لم تزالوا متصفين بالظلم , ومنه سؤالكم هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The faithful group were God’s servants, whom the condemned had treated as weak and thought little of separating from; they continued believing in all the messengers’ teachings by God’s command.
rows.anchor: أي ناس استضعفتموهم فهان عليكم فراقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The believers affirm all that the messengers brought, then ask forgiveness to cover their shortcomings; God’s forgiveness makes the sin forgotten by everyone, even the recording angels.
rows.anchor: أي استر إيماننا عيوبنا التي كان تقصيرنا بها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They ask God to act toward them with the good of mercy; He is the best of the merciful because His mercy saves the sincere believer from misery, humiliation, and unbelief.
rows.anchor: لأنك تخلص من رحمته من كل شقاء وهوان

rows.speaker: الشهاب السمين
rows.claim: Al-Samin distinguishes ḍamma sukhriyyan, derived from service or subjection, from kasra sukhriyyan, derived from mockery; the form intensifies the association in either reading.
rows.anchor: السخرة - بالضم : الاستخدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By occupying themselves with mockery of the believers, they caused themselves to forget God’s remembrance and failed to fear Him in His devoted servants.
rows.anchor: أي لأنهم كانوا السبب في ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They devoted their powers to mocking those believers, so their laughter at anything else counted as nothing.
rows.anchor: كأنهم لما صرفوا قواهم إلى الاستهزاء بهم عد ضحكهم من غيرهم عدما

none: The segment only quotes verses 24:20–22 and contains no commentary.
